$comment: Acceptance-test deck. Exercises 13 of the 18 archetypes with real Channelplay content. All copy is deliberately brand-compliant: sentence case, no exclamation marks, no placeholder phrases, no forbidden text.

slides.title: Retail execution, measured
slides.subtitle: How Channelplay runs field programmes that hold up under audit

slides.title: Where retail programmes break
slides.kicker: Most field programmes fail on execution, not on strategy. The plan is sound and the store still looks wrong on a Tuesday afternoon.

slides.title: The gap between the plan and the shelf
slides.deck: Three failure modes account for most of the loss we see when we take over a programme.
slides.body:
Attrition is the first. Field roles turn over faster than they can be trained, so the person in the store on any given day is often the least experienced person who has ever worked it.

The second is unverified reporting. When a promoter self-reports compliance with no evidence attached, the number that reaches the brand is a measure of optimism rather than of what is on the shelf.

The third is latency. A monthly report describes a month that is already gone. By the time a stock-out is visible in a dashboard, the sale is lost and the shopper has bought a competitor.

slides.title: How we staff and train
slides.kicker: The programme is only as good as the person standing in the store. We treat that person as the product.

slides.title: From hire to certified, in four steps

steps.body: Video modules and instructor-led sessions delivered to the field app, completed before the first store visit.
Two supervised days in a live store with a certified peer, scored against a fixed rubric.
One day a month back in the classroom for refreshers, new launches and objection handling.
Training scores, trainer feedback, store feedback and customer outcomes combine into a single certification level.

slides.title: What certification changes
slides.intro: Certification is not a badge. It gates which stores a person can work, and it is re-earned every quarter.

cells.subtitle: Store tiering
cells.body: Only level three and above are deployed to flagship and high-value doors.

cells.subtitle: Pay linkage
cells.body: Certification level feeds directly into the incentive band, so training has a cash consequence.

cells.subtitle: Attrition signal
cells.body: A level that stops progressing is the earliest reliable predictor we have of a resignation.

cells.subtitle: Client visibility
cells.body: The brand sees the certification mix of the team working its stores, refreshed weekly.

slides.title: The technology layer
slides.kicker: Every claim a programme makes should be traceable to evidence captured at the point it happened.

stages.label: Capture
stages.body: Geo-stamped photo and form capture in the field app, offline tolerant

stages.label: Verify
stages.body: Automated image checks flag staged, duplicated or out-of-window submissions

stages.label: Score
stages.body: Compliance scored against the planogram and the visit checklist

stages.label: Alert
stages.body: Stock-outs and compliance breaks raised the same day to the responsible supervisor

stages.label: Report
stages.body: Brand dashboards refresh continuously against the verified record

slides.title: What each audience gets
slides.intro: The same verified record, presented differently depending on who is acting on it.

columns.subtitle: Field team
columns.body: A route for the day, the checklist for each store, and immediate feedback on whether a submission was accepted.

columns.subtitle: Supervisor
columns.body: Exceptions only. Who did not check in, which stores failed compliance, and which stock-outs are still open.

columns.subtitle: Brand manager
columns.body: Coverage, compliance and availability by territory, with the underlying evidence one click away.

columns.subtitle: Finance
columns.body: Headcount, attendance and incentive exposure reconciled against the same attendance record the field sees.

slides.title: What we commit to, and how it is checked
slides.intro: Every commitment below is measured from the verified record, not from self-reporting.

slides.title: Compliance improves once evidence is required
slides.deck: Audited compliance across a national FMCG programme, before and after evidence capture was made mandatory.
slides.body:
The step change is not the result of better people. It is the result of a claim becoming checkable.

Self-reported compliance barely moved. Audited compliance rose because the gap between the two stopped being invisible.

slides.title: From a national account review
slides.quote: The difference was not that the numbers got better. It was that we finally believed them.
